content.comment_body: Hi [user_name], I have a [article_no] device running as a webserver, and each day I need to log in multiple times just to interact with the F1-F4 buttons. Functionality is fine, but the frequent logouts, sometimes occurring just seconds after logging in, are really inconvenient. For context, I'm using a web user account with no password (pw left blank), and I've tried selecting 'Keep me logged on', but nothing seems to help. I’ve searched for solutions but haven’t found any information on this issue. Because I'm accessing it via mobile network, having to reload the login page every time is very frustrating. Any suggestions or help would be greatly appreciated!
Is it possible your internet provider disconnects you every 24 hours and that’s causing the logout?
No, that’s not the case. If I log in with 'remember me', as soon as I close and reopen the page, it asks me to log in again.
Same for me. All I have to do is press "Login" and I'm logged back in—no need to re-enter the password.

Same situation here, but on mobile networks the login screen takes time to load, then I have to press the login button and wait for it to load again. By then, I could have already pressed the F button! Maybe I'm just too impatient? Haha.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are frustrated with the webserver’s ‘Keep me logged on’ or ‘remember me’ feature, as it still requires frequent login, especially after closing and reopening the web page. This inconvenience is amplified on mobile networks because of extra loading times. Overall, users want the login session to be more persistent and for access to be smoother when the web application is used repeatedly throughout the day.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the webserver to preserve their login session when ‘Keep me logged on’ or ‘remember me’ is used, allowing seamless access even after closing and reopening the page, so that interaction is faster and does not require repeated authentication.
